path_decisions.rationale: Mean reversion uses volume_threshold=0.8 (lower than trend's 1.0) — but mean_rev requires RSI+BB+volume simultaneously (line 95), the volume filter is too weak and may admit low-quality signals

Mean reversion RSI oversold=30/overbought=70 (line 30-31) is standard but crypto RSI often stays extreme >40/<60 for extended periods. Wider thresholds (25/75) would capture more extreme oversold/overbought conditions for higher-quality mean-reversion entries

SignalGenerator.consolidate_signals() uses simple net-vote (line 63-69) — conflicting LONG+SHORT signals cancel to FLAT, losing valid directional information. A confidence-weighted vote would preserve strong signals

PositionSizer.size() uses win_rate=0.5 hardcoded default (line 39) regardless of actual strategy performance — Kelly sizing with wrong win_rate produces suboptimal position sizes that hurt win-rate PnL

candidate_solution.summary: 4 changes: (1) increase mean_rev volume_threshold, (2) widen RSI extremes for mean_rev, (3) confidence-weighted signal consolidation, (4) use actual win_rate for Kelly sizing

change_1.title: Increase mean_reversion volume_threshold from 0.8 to 1.0 for higher-quality signals
change_1.current: volume_threshold=0.8 — allows entries even when volume is below average, admitting weak mean-reversion setups
change_1.proposed: Raise default to volume_threshold=1.0 (same as trend_following). Volume confirmation is more important for mean-reversion because the thesis requires strong volume to validate the reversal. Add to param_space with range [0.8, 1.5].
change_1.rationale: Mean reversion signals at oversold levels need volume confirmation to distinguish genuine reversals from continuation dips. Volume below average (threshold=0.8) at oversold levels often signals continued selling pressure, not reversal. Requiring above-average volume filters out false bottoms.

change_2.title: Widen RSI extreme thresholds for mean-reversion quality
change_2.current: rsi_oversold=30, rsi_overbought=70 — standard equity thresholds that miss crypto extremes
change_2.proposed: Change defaults to rsi_oversold=25, rsi_overbought=75 for mean_reversion only (not trend_following). Crypto markets exhibit more extreme RSI readings that persist longer. Mean-reversion entries at RSI<25 (not 30) are higher conviction because the instrument is truly oversold, not just trending down. Include in param_space with ranges [20,35] and [65,80].
change_2.rationale: RSI 30 in a downtrend often means 'still falling' in crypto, not 'about to reverse'. RSI below 25 is a much stronger oversold signal that historically has higher reversal probability. The extra 5 points of RSI waiting increases per-trade win rate significantly for mean-reversion strategies.

change_3.title: Replace net-vote signal consolidation with strength-weighted voting
change_3.current: consolidate_signals() sums direction.value (+1/-1) and cancels to FLAT when net=0. Two weak signals (0.3 strength each) override one strong signal (0.9 strength).
change_3.proposed: Replace with weighted vote: net = sum(s.direction.value * s.strength). Direction = sign of net. Strength = |net| / sum(strengths). This preserves strong directional conviction even when offset by weak opposing signals. Also add a min_strength threshold (default=0.3) below which consolidated signals are discarded.
change_3.rationale: Current unweighted vote treats all signals equally. If trend_following produces a strong LONG (0.8 strength) and mean_reversion produces a weak SHORT (0.4 strength) at the same symbol, they cancel to FLAT — losing the strong conviction. Weighted consolidation lets the strong conviction through, directly improving win_rate by acting on higher-confidence signals.

change_4.title: Use per-strategy actual win_rate for Kelly position sizing instead of hardcoded 0.5
change_4.current: win_rate=0.5 hardcoded default — PositionSizer ignores actual strategy performance, over-sizing strategies with low win_rate and under-sizing high win_rate strategies
change_4.proposed: Add strategy_win_rates dict to PositionSizer.__init__(). When sizing a signal, look up strategy_id in strategy_win_rates. If found, use actual win_rate. If not, fall back to 0.5. The strategy_win_rates should be populated from BacktestResult.win_rate after the first backtest run for each strategy.
change_4.rationale: Kelly criterion is extremely sensitive to win_rate input. Using 0.5 for a strategy with actual 0.45 win_rate leads to over-betting (positions too large), increasing loss severity on losing trades. Using 0.5 for a 0.60 win_rate strategy leads to under-betting (positions too small), leaving profit on the table. Correct Kelly sizing directly affects PnL and indirectly win_rate through better risk/reward calibration.

notes: Volume filtering is inconsistent across strategies: trend uses 1.0x average, mean_rev uses 0.8x, volatility_breakout uses 1.5x surge. This inconsistency suggests none are optimally tuned. The signal consolidation issue (unweighted vote) is particularly impactful when multiple strategies disagree — the current cancel-to-FLAT behavior discards high-confidence signals, which hurts win_rate because the best opportunities (strong consensus) are being ignored in favor of the weakest (even split).
